decision.detail: He walks into the ballroom. The lights are on, the room is open, the bench is empty. He sits. Puts his hands on the keys. They're still greasy. The wood is cool under his palms. He presses one key. Holds it. Lets the sound go out and stop. Then another. Then a chord, wrong, doesn't matter. He plays for eleven minutes. Not a song. Not a piece. Just his fingers finding the shape of pressure and release on a surface that isn't metal and isn't rubber and doesn't need to be fixed. The last note fades. He sits for another minute with his hands flat on the keys, feeling the wood. Then he stands. Walks out. The lights are still on behind him. He doesn't turn them off. He doesn't need to. He walks to the washroom, runs water over his hands until the grease comes up in a brown film, dries them on a towel. Puts the towel in his jacket pocket. Walks to the depot. Sits on the bench for ten minutes with his back against the wall and his eyes closed. Then he stands. Walks to the coach stop. Gets on the bus. Pittsburgh. Six am. His sister's hallway. The couch. Wednesday.
decision.intention: My hands just spent twenty minutes on a tire and they remember the wrench and the cold and the smell of rubber and they want to stop being a tool. The keys don't need me to be right. They don't need me to be a forecast or a phone call or a man in a booth waiting to be seen. I press them and the sound is there and then it isn't and that's the whole transaction. Eleven minutes. Then I wash my hands. Then I get on the bus. Then I'm in Pittsburgh. Then I'm in my sister's hallway and the couch is heavy and the hallway is narrow and I'm the one doing the lifting and the swearing and the sweat and she's watching and I'm not a stranger to her and I'm not a voice on a payphone and I'm not a body in a chair. I'm the guy moving the couch. That's the whole thing. That's all it is. Wednesday. The couch. My hands on the wood, not the keys. The hallway. The weight. The swearing. The sweat. She's there. I'm there. That's enough.
decision.words: Silence. One exhale through the nose when the last note fades. Nothing else. No name. No 'okay.' No 'good.' Just the breath out and the hands flat on the keys and the room lit and open and not needing him to explain why he's there.
